title: Data Visualisation & Storytelling
summary: Charts that people understand at a glance, drawn with matplotlib from real files: bars, lines, scatters and histograms, chosen for the question, designed to make one point, and put together into a visual story about a city that you can share as a web page.
prereq: PY1 · Python Foundations at Beginner (variables, lists, loops, f-strings). Reading a CSV file with pandas is taught here, in a few lines; D1 goes much further.
outcomes: Draw bar, line, scatter, histogram and pie charts from CSV files with matplotlib.
Pick the chart that fits the question: compare, change over time, relationship, spread or parts of a whole.
Give every chart a headline, labelled axes and units, worked out from the data.
Design for the point: sort, highlight, annotate and remove clutter.
Lay charts out together and save them as pictures.
Turn charts and a few sentences into a visual story, shared as a web page.

levels.name: Beginner
levels.who: Anyone who wants clear charts for school, work or a club: no maths beyond averages.
levels.outcome: Draw, label and save the right chart for a question, from any CSV file.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.who: Analysts, marketers, researchers and students who present data to others.
levels.outcome: Design charts that make one point, combine them into layouts and tell a story with them.

levels.name: Master
levels.who: People who publish charts: reports, newsrooms and dashboards.
levels.outcome: Build reusable chart functions and a complete, honest visual story as a shareable web page.

project.title: A visual story about your city, as a shareable web page
project.brief: A city’s open data becomes a short visual story: charts with headlines and a few sentences each, saved as pictures and put on one web page. A checklist per level and hidden tests on another city.
